content: 1. M. Kwik, G. Gronvall, E. Brunson, T. Kirk Sell, S. Ravi, and colleagues authored a document titled How to steward medical countermeasures and public trust in an emergency – a communication casebook for FDA and its public health partners. This document was accessed on July 27, 2017. 2. A final report was published on community engagement and case analysis methods for developing post-incident risk communication strategies in response to intentional biological environmental contamination incidents. This report was accessed on July 27, 2017. 3. T. Sellnow, A.N. Miller, L. Neuberger, A. Todd, and R. Freihau conducted an evidence synthesis to support the WHO Guidelines on Emergency Risk Communication. Their work focused on how to best develop and sustain emergency risk communication staff capacity for preparedness and response. This was published by the University of Central Florida in 2017. 4. J. William, M. Nocera, and C. Casteel conducted a systematic review on the effectiveness of disaster training for healthcare workers, published in the Annals of Emergency Medicine in 2008. 5. D. De Roeck provided a guidance note on the use of oral cholera vaccines, which was accessed on July 27, 2017. 6. L. Gautier analyzed a community-led infection prevention strategy adopted in preparation for the Ebola virus disease response. This analysis was published by the International Rescue Committee in 2016. 7. M. Francia documented how social mobilizers empowered hotspot communities to combat Ebola in Sierra Leone. This was accessed on July 27, 2017. 8. D. Toppenberg-Pejcic provided evidence to support the WHO Guideline on Emergency Risk Communication, focusing on ensuring sufficient and sustainable financing for emergency risk communication. This was accessed on August 22, 2017. 9. S. Wilkinson shared lessons learned from using media and communication to respond to public health emergencies during the Ebola outbreak. This was published as a practice briefing and accessed on July 27, 2017. 10. The Sierra Leone YMCA conducted an evaluation of its emergency response to the Ebola outbreak, with findings published in a report accessed on July 27, 2017. 11. Communication challenges and good practices during the Ebola outbreak in Liberia and Sierra Leone were documented in reports published in 2015 and accessed on July 27, 2017. 12. D. Padgett, P. Sopory, J. Nickell, A. Day, L.L. Wilkins, K.S. Eckert, and colleagues synthesized evidence to support the WHO Guideline on Emergency Risk Communication, focusing on the elements and steps of effective strategic communication planning. This was accessed on August 22, 2017. 13. J. Fielding, T. Allen, B. Chu, J. Galdo, and H.S. Gayle contributed to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) Ebola Response, with a report accessed on July 27, 2017. 14. The WHO Emergency Reform Workshop report on emergency risk communication was accessed on July 27, 2017. 15. M.M. Turner, H. Shaikh, and R. Rimal documented lessons in crisis communication from the Ebola risk communication project in Liberia. This was accessed on July 27, 2017. 16. C. Sugg highlighted the role of communication in powering global health in a report accessed on July 27, 2017. 17. The Africa APPG inquiry examined community-led health systems and the Ebola outbreak, with findings published in a report accessed on July 27, 2017. 18. M.-P. Allie, R. Colebunders, V. de Clerck, and J. Gabaldon conducted a medico-operational review of the Ebola response, with findings published in a report accessed on July 27, 2017. 19. J. Anoko used an anthropological approach to study communication with rebellious communities during the Ebola outbreak in Guinea. This was accessed on July 31, 2017. 20. ACF Sierra Leone published a case study on community-led Ebola management and eradication (CLEME), focusing on triggering behavioral change to strengthen community resilience. This was accessed on July 31, 2017. 21. K.S. Eckert, P. Sopory, A. Day, L.L. Wilkins, D. Padgett, J. Novak, and colleagues synthesized evidence to support the WHO Guideline on Emergency Risk Communication, focusing on the best social media channels and practices to promote health protection measures and dispel misinformation during public health emergencies. This was accessed on August 22, 2017. 22. N. Modarres conducted a qualitative study on community perspectives about Ebola in Bong, Lofa, and Montserrado counties of Liberia, with findings published in a final report accessed on July 31, 2017. 23. A community-focused intervention in Sierra Leone, titled Hotspot Nusters, was documented and accessed on July 31, 2017. 24. M. Kamai-Yanni emphasized the importance of building resilient health systems and learning from the Ebola crisis in a report accessed on July 31, 2017. 25. D. Rubyan-Ling explored diaspora communications and health-seeking behavior during the Ebola outbreak, with findings from the Sierra Leonean community in London published in a briefing paper accessed on July 31, 2017. 26. L.L. Wilkins, P. Sopory, A. Day, S. Eckert, D. Padgett, J. Novak, and colleagues synthesized evidence to support the WHO Guideline on Emergency Risk Communication, focusing on the elements and timing of messages to influence public concern and motivate health-protective actions. This was accessed on August 22, 2017. 27. D. Abramson and R.S. Piltch-Loeb studied public perceptions of Zika risk, including awareness, knowledge, and receptivity to public health interventions, with findings published in a report accessed on July 31, 2017. 28. S. Wilkinson, L.S. Upham, S.A. Pennington, S. O'Reilly, D. Asproloupos, H.D. McIntyre, and colleagues examined responsibility for the care of women during and after pregnancies affected by gestational diabetes, with findings published in the Medical Journal of Australia in 2014. 29. D. Toppenberg-Pejcic, J. Noyes, T. Allen, N. Alexander, M. Vanderford, and G. Gamhewage conducted a rapid grey literature evidence review to support the WHO Guideline on Emergency Risk Communication. This was accessed on July 31, 2017. 30. B. Shea, J. Grimshaw, G. Wells, M. Boers, N. Andersson, C. Hamel, and colleagues developed the AMSTAR tool to assess the methodological quality of systematic reviews, with findings published in BMC Medical Research Methodology in 2007. 31. The Cochrane Effective Practice and Organisation of Care (EPOC) group provided suggested risk of bias criteria for EPOC reviews, which were accessed on July 31, 2017. 32. E. Davids and N. Roman conducted a systematic review of the relationship between parenting styles and children's physical activity, with findings published in the African Journal of Physical Health Education, Recreation, and Dance in 2014. 33. The Critical Appraisal Skills Programme (CASP) provided a qualitative checklist, which was accessed on July 31, 2017. 34. The Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) was made available online and accessed on July 31, 2017. 35. J. Tyndall presented a paper on the hierarchy of grey literature at the Australian Library and Information Association Biennial Conference in 2008, which was accessed on July 31, 2017.
